With consent of learned counsel for the appellant, heard finally at motion stage.

2. This appeal has been filed by the claimant/appellant under Section 173 of the Motor Vehicles Act,
1988 against the award dated 12.01.2019 passed in MACC No.178/2013 by 4th Additional M.A.C.T.,
Katni District- Katni seeking setting aside of impugned award and grant of suitable compensation.
3. Learned counsel for the appellant submits that though in claim petition income of appellant is mentioned as Rs.5000/- per month.

But appellant has deposed in his examination-in-chief that he Sunil Kumar Dubey vs Ravind Jitendra on 14 May, 2024 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/104765941/

sentences.text: Further in his cross examination also appellant has stated that he was earning Rs.3000/-.
This fact has been reiterated by appellant Sunil Dubey in para 12 and 13 of his cross examination.
It is also urged that evidence adduced in the Court would prevail over pleadings in the claim petition.
Therefore, Tribunal has wrongly dismissed appellant's claim petition on the ground that in view of income of appellant, claim petition under Section 163 A of Motor Vehicle Act is not maintainable.
Therefore, appeal filed by the appellant be allowed and impugned award be set aside and suitable compensation be awarded.
4. I have heard learned counsel for the appellant and perused record of the case.
5. Present claim petition has been filed by appellant/claimant under Section 163 A of Motor Vehicle Act and in column 6 of petition, income of appellant is mentioned as Rs.5000/- per month.
Evidently, only those claim petitions are maintainable under Section 163 A of Motor Vehicle Act wherein claimant's annual income is not more than Rs.40,000/- per annum.

6. It is correct that appellant/claimant Sunil Kumar Dubey has deposed in examination in chief that he was earning Rs.3000/- per month and in para 12 and 13 of cross examination also appellant has stated that he was earning Rs.3000/- per month.
7.

In this Court's considered opinion, with respect to maintainability of claim petition under Section 163 A of Motor Vehicle Act, pleadings in claim petition are of vital importance and determining factor.
Maintainability of claim petition cannot be decided on the basis of evidence led by claimant.
It has to be decided on the basis of pleadings in the claim petition itself.
Hence, evidence adduced by claimant would not prevail over pleadings in claim petition.
In view of income of claimant as mentioned in claim petition, claimant's claim petition under Section 163 A of Motor Vehicle Act is not maintainable.
8. Therefore, in view of findings recorded by tribunal in para 14 of impugned award are proper and cannot be said that they are perverse and contrary to pleadings in claim petition or against law.

Therefore, no interference is required in findings recorded by the tribunal.
9.
Hence, appeal filed by appellant is dismissed of accordingly.
